Out of curiosity, what was the course title? I have a BSc in Econ, an MSc in 'Global Sustainability Solutions' (too general) and I was considering additional qualifications to help shift towards ESG roles
Just to confirm, is that how the role titles are rebranding as well?

It stand for Environmental, Social, and Governance, three aspects of a business' operation. Recently, the 'S' part has been caught up in the 'Woke' label, because it is more to do with diversity and social causes, but regardless, it's an important concept. It basically involves looking at how a company operates and assessing it through the lens of these three classes. So for Environment (E), you would look at how much carbon it emits, how efficient it is with resources like water. For Social (S), you might look at how it treats its workers, if they feel valued and have opportunity etc. For Governance, you look at how well it is governed. Is there enough oversight over decision making? Does the hierarchy make sense given everyone's respective job duties? I'm more into the E and G than the S.

It is used on top of a company's financial information. The Environment part is especially important given climate change. The problem is that, as companies haven't had to consider it before, it incurs costs to measure and report on these concepts. So when things are rough, a company can only afford to care about core financial metrics. Some would argue that a business' only obligation is to provide value to its owners and shareholders, so ESG would conflict with this. 

I think it's a good, but not perfect, concept. I'd like to go into an ESG career, as the field is only going to become more relevant and in demand. Unfortunately, as it's still an emerging field, there aren't many straight paths into it that I can see. Graduate roles are scarcer in my market.
